values.value: How much customer data sits behind your sends — roughly how many contact properties are in use, and do you have custom objects as well as contacts and companies?
How much audience data there is, and how many pieces it is in

[{"value":1,"label":"Contacts and companies with mostly HubSpot-standard properties; a few dozen custom properties at most, and no custom objects."},{"value":2,"label":"A few hundred custom properties in use, deals or tickets read by marketing, and perhaps one or two custom objects."},{"value":3,"label":"Custom properties in the high hundreds or more, several custom objects with their own associations, and calculated or rollup properties feeding segmentation."}]
Settings then Properties gives you the count per object, and Data Model lists any custom objects.

migration-accelerator/capabilities/platforms/hubspot.yaml — object_catalog.crm_data_model: contact_properties with its calculation and rollup subtypes, companies, deals, tickets, custom_objects and associations. The base wording asked about "30-100 tables, moderate SQL", which is Marketing Cloud's Data Extension vocabulary and doubly wrong here, since this target's person model is Data Cloud's Unified Individual rather than a table count at all. What is COUNTED is the same as on hubspot__sfmc and unchanged by that: the client has the properties and objects they have. Whether the model must be resolved into a unified profile before anything can be configured is slot 5's substituted question on this pair, and is not asked again here.
